Tabs.__init__ in generated src/textual/widgets/tabs.py:229-242 has the same parameter names, order and defaults as reference tabs.py:199-212 (tabs, active_tab=None, active_tab_style='#f0f0f0 on #021720', active_bar_style='#1BB152', inactive_tab_style, inactive_bar_style='#455058', inactive_text_opacity=0.5, animation_duration=0.3, animation_function='out_cubic', tab_padding=None, search_by_first_character=True).

Non-blocking divergences in internal names: TabsRenderable.__init__ takes positional bar_position (tabs.py:91) versus the reference's keyword-only bar_offset; the private _Edge helper (tabs.py:64) replaces the reference's change of _layout_resolve.Edge to a NamedTuple (reference _layout_resolve.py:21). criteria.deficiency: None blocking. Divergences listed in evidence are internal and do not break the Tabs public API.

evidence: tabs.py imports upward only from its own layer: ..events, .._layout_resolve, ..keys, ..reactive, ..renderables.opacity, ..renderables.underline_bar, ..widget (tabs.py:8-14).
renderables/opacity.py imports only rich and textual.renderables._blend_colors (base opacity.py:1-8, unchanged); renderables do not import widgets.
_layout_resolve is imported by layouts/dock.py and layouts/grid.py in the base, so importing it from a widget is an existing pattern.
Reference diff does not touch widgets/__init__.py or any registry, so no export registration is required; the patch correctly does not add one.

Tabs implements the Widget hooks used by the reference: render() (tabs.py:389), watch__active_tab_name (tabs.py:347), action_range_clicked (tabs.py:339), with the same action string format range_clicked('<name>') (tabs.py:162).
Docs page added as the repo's docs/reference convention requires (docs/reference/tabs.md).
No new third-party dependency: the patch imports only rich (already pinned, pyproject rich ^11.2.0), typing, and in-repo modules.
Style(meta=...) and Text.stylize, which the patch uses, are standard rich APIs already used by the reference.

Style blending lives in the renderable layer: blend_style (opacity.py:40-59) is used by Opacity.__rich_console__ (opacity.py:35) and by Tabs' inactive-label styling (tabs.py:144), so the blend logic has a single source.
Click metadata is produced in UnderlineBar (underline_bar.py:100-102) from name->span mappings supplied by the widget, keeping the widget free of rendering internals.
Widget logic (active tab, keyboard, animation) stays in widgets/tabs.py (on_key tabs.py:360, watch tabs.py:347).

Layout uses the existing layout_resolve protocol through a structurally conforming _Edge (tabs.py:64-71, call at tabs.py:131), not a parallel layout algorithm. The reference instead changed the shared Edge type (reference _layout_resolve.py:21) to make it instantiable; the patch avoids touching that shared type.
Animation uses Widget.animate with the existing easing names (tabs.py:347 via animation_function), and reactivity uses Reactive plus the watch__ convention (tabs.py:226-227).

Tabs.on_key overrides Widget.on_key (base widget.py:356) without calling dispatch_key (base widget.py:357). The reference does the same (reference tabs.py:233), so this is a shared gap, not a patch-specific deviation.
criteria.deficiency: None relative to the reference. The shared on_key override bypasses Widget.dispatch_key, but the reference does the same.

evidence: Focus changes go through the public App API: await self.app.set_focus(None) (tabs.py:378), matching the async signature at base app.py:306 and the other callers in base widget.py:317 and view.py:237.
Renderables do not reach into widget state; TabsRenderable receives only plain values (tabs.py:91-112).
Keyboard and click handling uses action strings resolved by the existing action dispatch (action_range_clicked tabs.py:339), with no transport or persistence leakage.
Google-style docstrings with Args/Returns sections, matching base widget/opacity docstrings (tabs.py:21-31, opacity.py:40-53, underline_bar.py:17-24).

Private helpers and constants use underscore prefixes (_Edge tabs.py:64, _DIGIT_KEYS tabs.py:18, _get_blended_color_cached opacity.py:63), consistent with the base's _blend_colors and _layout_resolve naming.
Tests follow tests/<pkg>/test_*.py with an __init__.py per package, matching tests/renderables/__init__.py.
Tab is a plain class rather than the reference's dataclass; the constructor and equality surface is equivalent, so this is not a convention violation.

Keyboard: next/previous wrap (tabs.py:290-296); digits map to 1-based tabs with 0 meaning the 10th or last (tabs.py:321-337); first-character search wraps and skips the active tab (tabs.py:300-319); Escape unfocuses (tabs.py:378).
Duplicate names: the first occurrence keeps its position and the last label is shown (_displayed_tabs tabs.py:45-62, matching the reference's dict-based behavior at reference tabs.py:~140).
Click targets cover each tab's full padded span, including padding (selection_ranges in TabsRenderable.__rich_console__, tabs.py:136 onward), and active tabs carry no @click action.
Auto-fit padding distributes leftover width via layout_resolve (tabs.py:113-134); fixed tab_padding bypasses it.
Underline interpolates between label ranges with wrap-around (tabs.py:136 onward), and animates to the displayed index (tabs.py:347-357).

Patch is stricter in one place: the reference's Escape calls set_focus without await (reference tabs.py:248), while the patch awaits it. The patch also uses the displayed index for the bar, where the reference's full-list index can overrun its de-duplicated label list.
